committed: Before any implementation output was inspected: this file and the validation contract in ASTROMETRY.md were committed ahead of js/measure/astrometric-series.js, the validation tool, the oracle's inputs, script and results, and every test. A check that a measurement crosses is a failed check, not a reason to move the bound; only Carl resets a threshold, with a register row. Where a bound rests on an approximation, the approximation is named here and the bound is the width it justifies, fixed before any number existed.

definition.what: Positions of one source at several epochs, fitted over time: a proper motion linear in time, a two-epoch shift under a fixed-motion assumption, and a joint fit of parallax and proper motion that is permitted only when the epochs sample the parallactic ellipse.
definition.plane: standard (tangent-plane, gnomonic) coordinates xi east and eta north about a reference direction (the normalised mean of the positions' unit vectors, or one the caller names), in arcseconds. All fits are weighted linear least squares on the two coordinates of each epoch with the stated, independent, per-axis uncertainties (arcseconds on the sky).
definition.properMotion: xi(t) = x0 + mux (t - tRef), eta(t) = y0 + muy (t - tRef); tRef the inverse-variance-weighted mean epoch; mu in arcseconds per Julian year (365.25 days); mux is the proper motion in right ascension times cos(dec)
definition.jointModel: the same plus parallax: xi(t) += p fx(t), eta(t) += p fy(t), with fx = X sin(a) - Y cos(a) and fy = X cos(a) sin(d) + Y sin(a) sin(d) - Z cos(d) for the Earth's barycentric position (X, Y, Z) in au in the equatorial frame at the epoch and (a, d) the reference direction; p in arcseconds, so the distance is 1/p parsecs
definition.earth: the Earth's geocentre relative to the solar-system barycentre, at a TDB Julian date: the repository's ephemeris pack (js/data/ephemeris/solarSystem2025.js, Earth heliocentric, ecliptic of J2000, 2025-01-01 to 2045-01-01 TDB) plus the Sun's offset from the barycentre, the mass-weighted sum of the heliocentric positions of Venus, the Earth, Mars and the Jupiter system (all from the pack) and of Saturn, Uranus and Neptune (from the sky kernel's Standish elements), rotated to the equator by the obliquity 23.439291111 degrees; no fetch, no other ephemeris
definition.timeScales: an epoch is a value with a format (jd or mjd) and a scale (utc, tt or tdb); it is converted to TDB Julian date: TT = UTC + 69.184 s (TAI - UTC = 37 s; refused for UTC before 2017-01-01), TDB = TT + 0.001657 sin(g) + 0.000014 sin(2g) seconds with g = 357.53 + 0.98560028 (JD - 2451545) degrees
definition.frameStatement: every parallax and every distance carries the reference-frame statement: the parallax is relative to the reference frame of the positions (the reference stars of the calibration), not absolute; a correction to absolute is applied only when the caller supplies its size and its source (no default, no universal value), and is then shown with both; a distance from a relative parallax is stated as never smaller than the true distance if the reference stars' mean parallax is positive
definition.distance: d = 1/p parsecs; the interval is the image under p -> 1/p of the interval of p from the chi-square profile of the joint fit (Prompt 154's profileInterval, levels 0.6827 and 0.95): [1/p_hi, 1/p_lo], open above (null) when p_lo <= 0; no point value is shown when the parallax is not positive; a distance is never returned without its interval, its level, its method and its frame statement
definition.refusals: not-constrained objects: ok false, status 'not-constrained', a code, an English message and the data a page needs to say it in another language

joint.quadrants: the Earth's heliocentric ecliptic longitude at each epoch, in four 90 degree sectors from 0 degrees; at least 3 of the 4 sectors hold an epoch

twoEpoch.label: shift under a fixed-motion assumption; not a parallax

scene.synthetic: tools/astrometric-series-synth.mjs: a source at distance D = 1/p parsecs with a constant barycentric velocity tangent to the sky, seen from the Earth's barycentric position through the exact spherical geometry (the apparent direction is the normalised vector from the Earth to the source); positions are given as right ascension and declination with a seeded Gaussian error per axis; the truth manifest (position, proper motion, parallax, epochs, sigmas, seed) travels with every series
scene.epochWindow: an ensemble series draws its epochs uniformly at random in a window that starts at a random date between 2025-02-01 and 2040-01-01 TDB; a draw that fails the rules of the fit under test is drawn again and counted
scene.sky: right ascension uniform in [0, 360), sin(declination) uniform in [-0.99, 0.99]

a1.pmExact.what: noise-free linear motion in a stated tangent plane (reference direction passed in), five epochs between 2460700 and 2461800 TDB, recovered

a2.pmClosedForm.what: three epochs at 0, 1 and 3 years with xi = 0, 1, 2 arcsec and sigmas 1, 2, 1 arcsec, eta the negative, solved by hand: slope, intercept at tRef and their sigmas from the normal equations in rational arithmetic

a3.twoEpoch.what: the two-epoch shift: displacement and its uncertainty sqrt(s1^2 + s2^2) exactly; the label text above appears on every result and the result has no parallax and no distance field; a joint fit of the same two epochs refuses with code too-few-epochs

a4.parallaxFactors.what: the factors against closed forms on a synthetic circular Earth orbit of radius 1 au in the ecliptic (not the ephemeris): at the north ecliptic pole the ellipse is a circle of radius 1; on the ecliptic its semi-minor axis is 0 and its semi-major axis 1, along the ecliptic; at ecliptic latitude b the semi-minor axis is |sin b|

a5.jointNoiseless.what: one-year, well-sampled (24 epochs evenly spaced over 365 days from 2026-01-05, TDB), noise-free spherical truth through the pack's Earth: p = 0.12 arcsec, mu = (0.35, -0.18) arcsec/yr at ra 265, dec +62 and at ra 75, dec +22 (near the ecliptic), recovered with the same Earth; the model is linear in the tangent plane and the truth is exactly spherical, the difference being a term of order p times the offset (below a micro-arcsecond)

a6.timeScales.what: UTC to TDB for 2026-01-01 and 2030-07-01: TT - UTC = 69.184 s, TDB - TT below 0.0017 s, an MJD is a JD minus 2400000.5 exactly; UTC before 2017 refused

a7.profile.what: the chi-square profile of the parallax by refitting at fixed parallax equals the analytic quadratic of the joint fit at five parallaxes, and profileInterval of it equals the covariance interval

b1.earth.what: the pack-derived barycentric Earth (equatorial, au) against astropy's get_body_barycentric('earth') (ERFA epv00, built in, no download) at 365 TDB dates 20 days apart from 2025-01-05; and after removing the best straight line from each two-year window the remainder, which is what a parallax series can see

b2.jointCrossEphemeris.what: noise-free series made in Python (spherical truth, ERFA's Earth) fitted by Gravitas with the pack's Earth: star A ra 265 dec +62, p 0.12, mu (0.35, -0.18), 24 epochs over 2026; star B ra 75 dec +22, p 0.045, mu (-0.08, 0.06), 16 uneven epochs over 2027-03-01 to 2028-02-20

b3.jointVsScipy.what: noisy series made in Python with a fixed numpy seed (A: sigma 0.004 arcsec, B: 0.006, C: ra 150 dec -35, 40 epochs over 2026-2029, p 0.03, mu (1.2, -0.8), sigma 0.008), fitted by scipy.optimize.least_squares (method lm) on the exact spherical model with ERFA's Earth and by Gravitas on the same positions: the difference in each of p, mux, muy as a share of the formal sigma, the formal sigma of p, and chi-square

b4.pmVsCurveFit.what: the straight-line fit of the same series' tangent offsets (about the normalised mean direction) by scipy.optimize.curve_fit with absolute sigmas against Gravitas's proper-motion fit

b5.timeVsErfa.what: UTC to TT and TDB of 40 dates from 2025 to 2044 against astropy.time (ERFA, the leap-second table)

b6.authentic.what: an authentic series (published astrometry of a nearby star, or a frame sequence) under a fixed analysis contract; NOT RUN until Prompt 189 supplies authentic frames; nothing fetched, nothing fabricated or simulated

c1.jointCoverage.what: 3000 seeded series of 20 epochs in a 1.2-year window, sigma 0.01 arcsec per axis, p uniform in [0.02, 0.2] arcsec, mu uniform in [-1, 1] arcsec/yr per axis, the joint fit; the share of trials where the truth lies within 1 and 1.96 stated sigma of the estimate, for p, mux and muy

c2.distanceSymmetric.what: 3000 seeded series (sigma 0.005 arcsec, p = 0.1 arcsec, 20 epochs, as c1 otherwise): the share where the true distance 1/p lies in the stated distance interval at 0.6827 and at 0.95; the upper end is never open in this regime

c3.distanceAsymmetric.what: 3000 seeded series (sigma 0.01 arcsec, 20 epochs) with the true parallax set per series to 2.5 times the formal sigma of the parallax computed from the design: the share where the true distance lies in the stated interval at 0.6827 and 0.95 including the open ones; and over the series whose 0.6827 interval is closed, the mean of (d_hi - d) / (d - d_lo), which for a symmetric interval in p is (p + s) / (p - s) = 2.33 at p = 2.5 s: at least 1.5

c4.pmCoverage.what: 3000 seeded series of 6 epochs spread over 2 to 5 years, sigma 0.02 arcsec, mu uniform in [-1, 1] arcsec/yr, the proper-motion fit; the share of trials where the truth lies within 1 and 1.96 stated sigma, for mux and muy

c5.falseAlarm.what: the share of the c1 series and of the c4 series whose residuals fail the consistency test (p below 0.001) when the model is right

c6.shiftCoverage.what: 3000 seeded two-epoch series with no parallax (sigma 0.02 arcsec at each epoch, epochs 0.5 to 3 years apart, mu uniform in [-1, 1] arcsec/yr): the share where the true displacement lies within 1 and 1.96 stated sigma, for both axes

d1.jointRefusals.what: the joint fit refuses (not-constrained, the stated code and the numbers in data) a two-epoch series (too-few-epochs), seven epochs over a year (too-few-epochs), eight epochs over 0.5 year (span), eight epochs over 1.2 years that fall in two sectors only (phase-coverage), epochs identical (no-baseline); and solves one that meets the rules exactly (8 epochs, 0.9 year, 3 sectors): refusal codes exact

d2.twoEpochLabel.what: the label text appears on the result of every two-epoch call over 200 seeded pairs, however far apart the epochs are, and no result has a parallax or a distance

d3.wrongTimeScale.what: the epochs of a well-sampled year (24 epochs, sigma 0.004 arcsec, p = 0.15 arcsec) are all shifted by 45, 91.3, 182.6 and 273.9 days from the epochs the positions were made at (a wrong time scale or origin): at least 99 percent of 200 series each fail the consistency test, and the result's hints name the epoch time scale and its message contains the words time scale

d4.unitConfusion.what: a series whose epochs are Julian dates declared as modified Julian dates, and one whose epochs are modified Julian dates declared as Julian dates, are refused with code epoch-range and a message that names the format; a proper-motion fit (no ephemeris needed) of the same declared-wrong epochs is not refused for range

d5.outsideEphemeris.what: a series in 2010 (inside no ephemeris) is refused for the joint fit with code epoch-range and the pack's range in data, and its proper-motion fit works

d6.malformed.what: a non-finite position, a negative or zero sigma, an unknown scale or format, a declination beyond 90, an empty series, a position more than 3600 arcseconds from the others (too-wide) and more than 2000 epochs are each refused with the right code

d7.outlier.what: one epoch of 24 displaced by 12 sigma in a joint fit: at least 99 percent of 200 series fail the consistency test and the residual table's largest normalised residual is at that epoch in at least 95 percent

d8.frameStatement.what: over 200 seeded joint fits every parallax and every distance carries the frame statement (kind relative); a distance is always accompanied by its interval at both levels and its method; with a supplied correction without a source the fit refuses (correction-source); with one supplied the absolute parallax is the relative plus the correction and both are shown

d9.zeroParallax.what: 3000 seeded series (sigma 0.01 arcsec, 20 epochs, true parallax 0): the share whose 0.6827 distance interval is open above is the share of p estimates within one sigma of zero from above, 0.841; and no point distance is shown for a non-positive estimate

notRun: b6 until Prompt 189: no authentic series is held, none was fetched
corrections: 1: the oracle's nonlinear fit named scipy.optimize.least_squares method lm. Its first run stopped short of the minimum (chi-square 48.324 for series B where the minimum is 48.2985): the method's two-point difference step, 1.5e-8, is below what a double holds of an angle of order one radian, so the Jacobian was noise. This was found because the first Gravitas fit disagreed with it by 0.11 sigma in one proper-motion component, against the bound 0.1; the oracle was wrong and the module was right (the same fit by method trf with three-point differences and a step of 1e-4 reaches 48.29854, the module's 48.29853). The oracle was re-run with method trf; no bound, no case, no tolerance and no input was changed, and the first lm results were never committed
